steps.title: Import Angular Component decorator
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in the Component decorator that will be needed to create an Angular component.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a decorator
import { Injectable } from '@angular/core'
steps.expectedOutcome: The Component decorator is imported from @angular/core, making it available for creating Angular components.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've imported the Component decorator, which is essential for creating Angular components.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're importing Component from '@angular/core'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to use the import statement to bring in Component from '@angular/core'.

steps.title: Create the ListDemo component class
steps.instruction: Create a component class named ListDemo and decorate it with @Component. Include selector 'app-list-demo' and template 'ListDemo'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator above your class declaration. The decorator needs selector and template properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A ListDemo component class with @Component decorator, selector 'app-list-demo', and template 'ListDemo'
successCriteria: ListDemo class is created with @Component decorator containing selector 'app-list-demo' and template 'ListDemo'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the ListDemo component class with the correct decorator and metadata.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your component class is named ListDemo and includes both selector and template in the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to create a class named ListDemo with the @Component decorator that includes selector and template properties.

steps.title: Initialize the items array property
steps.instruction: Add an items property to the ListDemo component class that contains an array of sample objects with name and id properties
steps.hint: Create a property inside the class that holds an array of objects. Each object should have at least a name and id field for rendering purposes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ListDemo component will have an items property containing an array of sample data objects that can be used for list rendering
successCriteria: The ListDemo class contains an items property with an array of objects that have name and id properties
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created the items array property with sample data. This array will be used to demonstrate list rendering with Angular's structural directives.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your items array contains objects with both name and id properties for proper list rendering.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add an items property inside the ListDemo class that contains an array of objects with name and id fields.

steps.title: Create the component template with container
steps.instruction: Update the template property to include a main container div with an h2 heading that says 'My Items List'
steps.hint: Replace the simple div in the template with a more structured layout that includes a heading for your list
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: component template with heading template: `

Welcome

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a structured div with an h2 heading displaying 'My Items List'
successCriteria: Template includes a container div with an h2 element containing the text 'My Items List'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've created a proper container structure with a heading for your list component.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure your template includes both a container div and an h2 heading with the specified text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template needs to be updated with a container div that includes an h2 heading saying 'My Items List'.

steps.title: Add heading to display list title
steps.instruction: Inside the template string, add an h2 element with the text 'My Items List' above the existing div content.
steps.hint: Place the h2 element at the beginning of the template, before the div. Use the h2 HTML tag with descriptive text about the list.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: adding a heading to template

Product Catalog
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will include an h2 heading that describes the list content, providing context for what the user will see.
successCriteria: Template contains an h2 element with the text 'My Items List'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added a descriptive heading to your template. This helps users understand what the list will contain.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure you're using the h2 element with the exact text 'My Items List'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The heading isn't quite right. Add an h2 element inside the template with the text 'My Items List'.

steps.title: Create unordered list element
steps.instruction: Add a ul element inside the div container to hold the list items.
steps.hint: Place the ul element after the heading and inside the div. This will be the container for your list items.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains an unordered list element ready to hold the rendered items.
successCriteria: A ul element is added inside the div container after the heading.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added the ul element that will contain your list items. This creates the proper HTML structure for rendering lists.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the ul element is inside the div container and positioned after the heading.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ul element should be placed inside the div container, after the h2 heading. This will serve as the container for your list items.

steps.title: Add *ngFor directive to render list items
steps.instruction: Inside the ul element, add an li element with the *ngFor directive to iterate over the items array and display each item
steps.hint: Use *ngFor="let item of items" on the li element to loop through the array, then display {{item}} inside the li
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: using *ngFor to render a list
  • {{fruit}}
steps.expectedOutcome: The ul element contains an li element with *ngFor directive that will render each item from the items array
successCriteria: Li element is added inside ul with *ngFor directive that iterates over items array and displays each item using interpolation
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully added the *ngFor directive to render each item in the list. The structural directive will create one li element for each item in the array.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure the *ngFor directive is on the li element and uses the correct syntax: *ngFor="let item of items"
steps.feedbackWrong: The *ngFor directive should be added to an li element inside the ul. Use the syntax *ngFor="let item of items" and display {{item}} inside the li element.

steps.title: Display item properties using interpolation
steps.instruction: Replace the comment inside the li element with string interpolation to display each item value.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to display the item variable inside the li element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The list items will display the actual fruit names (Apple, Banana, Orange) instead of showing nothing.
successCriteria: The li element contains string interpolation {{ item }} to display each item value from the array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully used string interpolation to display each item in the list. The double curly braces {{ item }} tell Angular to output the current item's value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with interpolation, but make sure you're using the correct variable name 'item' that matches what you defined in the *ngFor directive.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to use string interpolation with double curly braces {{ }} and reference the 'item' variable that was created by the *ngFor directive.

steps.title: Add index tracking to *ngFor
steps.instruction: Modify the *ngFor directive to track the index of each item by adding 'index as i' to display both the index and item value
steps.hint: In Angular, you can access the index in *ngFor by using the syntax: *ngFor="let item of items; index as i". Then you can display both i and item in your template.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: tracking index in ngFor
  • {{idx}}: {{fruit}}
steps.expectedOutcome: The *ngFor directive will track the index and display it along with each item (e.g., '0: Apple', '1: Banana', '2: Orange')
successCriteria: The *ngFor directive includes 'index as i' and displays both the index and item value in the format 'i: item'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Excellent! You've successfully added index tracking to *ngFor. Now each list item shows its position in the array along with its value.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to add 'index as i' to your *ngFor directive and display both the index and item value in the template.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to modify the *ngFor directive to track the index using 'index as i' syntax, then display both the index and item value using interpolation.

steps.title: Style the list with basic CSS
steps.instruction: Add a styles property to the @Component decorator with CSS rules to style the list and list items.
steps.hint: Use the styles property array in the @Component decorator to add CSS rules for ul and li elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a styles property with CSS rules that enhance the visual appearance of the list.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator includes a styles property with CSS rules for styling the list elements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've added styles to enhance the visual presentation of your rendered list. The styles property allows you to add component-specific CSS rules.
steps.feedbackPartial: Good start! Make sure to add the styles property as an array within the @Component decorator with CSS rules for the list elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: Remember to add the styles property to the @Component decorator. Use an array format with CSS rules as strings to style your list elements.
